title: A Semantic Perception Framework for Robot Assistance Task Prediction in Agricultural Work Environments
content: Agricultural human robot collaboration requires perception systems that interpret both ongoing activity and the broader work conditions in which robotic assistance may be required. This work proposes a visual semantic framework for predicting three robot assistance categories, None, Material Handling, and Harvesting, from RGB images of agricultural work environments. The framework combines scene classification and object perception with a structured semantic representation integrating contextual, object level, segmentation derived, spatial, workload related, and higher level information. This representation captures complementary evidence from the observed agricultural scene. Scene classification was evaluated using ResNet50, EfficientNet B0, ViT B/16, and Swin Tiny, while canonical, lightweight modified, and modern detection and segmentation architectures were compared for object perception. ResNet50 was retained as the scene classifier, achieving a test Macro F1 of 84.31%, whereas YOLO11n Seg was selected for object perception with test box and mask mAP@0.5 values of 88.9% and 88.3%, respectively. For assistance prediction, five machine learning classifiers were evaluated across eight feature configurations. Bagging combined with the 64 feature Pepper harvest focus representation achieved the highest validation Macro F1 of 91.87%, improving the Scene only configuration by 10.35 percentage points and slightly outperforming the complete 77 feature representation. After validation based selection and train only refitting, the frozen model achieved 80.56% Accuracy, 80.06% Macro F1, and 80.94% Weighted F1 on the held out test subset. These results show that activity context is informative, while task oriented object, spatial, and semantic cues provide a richer basis for assistance prediction than scene context alone.
